papers.title: Homeostatic coupling of cortical and brainstem delta rhythms in sleeping infant rats.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: This study investigated the coupling between cortical and brainstem delta rhythms in sleeping infant rats. Sleep deprivation and hypercapnia perturbed delta power in both regions in lockstep, indicating strong homeostatic coupling.

papers.title: Feeding a Diurnal Rodent at Night Induces Weight Loss and Body Temperature Reduction Without Food-Anticipatory Activity.
papers.summary: The study examined whether the diurnal antelope ground squirrel exhibits food-anticipatory activity under time-restricted feeding, finding that nighttime food access caused weight loss, reduced activity, and hypothermia without FAA, indicating limited behavioral compensation in diurnal rodents.

papers.title: Shank3 mutation disrupts the molecular signature of sleepiness across development
papers.summary: This study used RNA-sequencing on Shank3ΔC mutant mice to investigate the molecular basis of sleepiness across development. The mutation blocked age-typical recruitment of sleep deprivation response pathways at P24 and in adulthood, while elevating oxidative stress pathways, indicating impaired molecular response to sleepiness.

papers.title: Systematic Review and Transcriptomic Meta-analysis of Environmental Enrichment Reveal Core Molecular Programs of Brain Plasticity.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis integrated transcriptomic data from 20 rodent studies of environmental enrichment, identifying consistent gene expression signatures related to synaptic function and plasticity, notably upregulation of activity-dependent transcription factors like Fos and Jun. The findings are accessible via an interactive web application, mEEtaBrain.

papers.title: Perinatal environmental enrichment affects murine neonates' brain structure before their active engagement with environment
papers.summary: This study used MRI to show that environmental enrichment alters brain structure in mouse neonates by postnatal day 7, with changes in hindbrain, dorsal striatum, and medial habenula. Maternal care differences partially mediated these effects.

papers.title: Novelty and anxiety differentially shape hippocampal assembly reactivation and sequence replay during REM sleep
papers.summary: This study combined calcium imaging and electrophysiology in mouse hippocampal CA1 neurons to detect reactivation during REM sleep. They found that structured waking activity is re-expressed during REM sleep, with novel experience enhancing sequential replay and anxiogenic experience increasing assembly reactivation frequency.

papers.title: Exercise modality-specific regulation of sleep stability in mice: An EEG-based comparative study of high-intensity interval training and moderate-intensity continuous training.
papers.summary: This EEG-based study compared high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) effects on sleep stability in mice. HIIT increased total sleep time, while MICT reduced sleep fragmentation and increased continuity, but direct modality differences were not statistically significant.

papers.title: Age-Associated Development of Sleep Disturbances in db/db Diabetic Mice.
papers.summary: The study characterizes age-dependent sleep disturbances in diabetic db/db mice, finding that NREM sleep fragmentation begins at 3 months of age with increased microarousals and reduced dark-phase wakefulness, associated with dysregulated sleep genes in subcortical regions.

papers.title: Chronic trazodone treatment consolidates sleep, improves memory, and reduces amyloid pathology in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease
papers.summary: Chronic trazodone treatment in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease consolidates sleep, improves memory, and reduces amyloid pathology, including a 45% reduction in hippocampal plaque burden in aged mice.

papers.title: Neferine improves sleep quality in chronically sleep-deprived mice by antagonizing OXRs in noradrenergic and serotonergic neurons.
papers.summary: This study in chronically sleep-deprived mice found that neferine (NEF), an alkaloid, improved sleep quality by increasing delta power and reducing fragmentation. Mechanistically, NEF antagonized orexin receptors in noradrenergic and serotonergic neurons, suppressing their activity and reducing norepinephrine and serotonin levels.

papers.title: Chemogenetic manipulation of mPFC neurons counteracts cognitive deficits but leaves sleep disturbances unaffected in a mouse model of chronic intermittent hypoxia.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: This study found that chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) caused hyperactivation in the infralimbic subregion of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) in mice. Chemogenetic inhibition of this region restored cognitive function and synaptic proteins but did not ameliorate sleep disturbances, indicating separate neural circuits for cognitive and sleep pathologies.

papers.title: Orexin Signaling, Glymphatic Clearance, and Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease: A Scoping Review and Hypothesis-Generating Conceptual Framework.
papers.summary: This scoping review evaluates evidence linking orexin signaling, glymphatic clearance, and preclinical Alzheimer's disease. It found limited human evidence for disease-modifying effects of dual orexin receptor antagonists, with preclinical findings preliminary and lacking human validation.

papers.title: Dyscoordination of thalamic reticular spindles is associated with social memory deficits in mice and humans with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.summary: This study examined the role of sleep spindles in social memory consolidation using mice and humans with autism spectrum disorder. They found that impaired spindles were associated with defective social memory, identified the sTRNPvalb-VPM circuit as essential for spindle generation, and developed machine learning models to predict autism based on spindle eigenvalues.

papers.title: Interactions between hippocampus and visceral organs in sleep and wakefulness.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: This study investigated synchronization between hippocampal neural activity and visceral signals (respiration, heart rate, stomach, duodenum) in cats during wakefulness and slow-wave sleep. They found that interoceptive signals reach the hippocampus in both states, with increased synchronization during SWS for respiratory and duodenal activities.

papers.title: The Internal Structure of Seizures Reflects Animal-Specific Trajectories of Disease Progression and Circadian Modulation in Epileptic Mice
papers.summary: This study analyzed long-term EEG recordings from epileptic mice, revealing that seizures follow structured sequences of burst states governed by sparse, animal-specific transition rules. Seizure microstructure evolves with disease progression and circadian phase, indicating a seizure grammar that consolidates over time.

papers.title: A neural signature of sleep deprivation in the human brain.
papers.summary: Using machine learning on large neuroimaging datasets, this study identified a neural signature that robustly distinguishes sleep-deprived from well-rested brains, validated across multiple independent datasets. The signature detects residual disturbances after recovery sleep, is sensitive to partial deprivation, and captures natural variations in sleep duration in the general population.

papers.title: Dynamic Changes in Glymphatic-Related Imaging Markers Across Acute Sleep Deprivation and Recovery in Healthy Young Adults.
papers.summary: This study in healthy young adults found that acute sleep deprivation (SD) altered glymphatic-related MRI markers, including decreased DTI-ALPS index and increased free water fraction, while recovery sleep partially reversed these changes. DTI-ALPS, free water fraction, and gBOLD-CSF coupling were identified as sensitive markers for SD and recovery.

papers.title: Sleep stage classification using instantaneous heart and breathing rates with a TCN-BiGRU-SE model.
papers.summary: The paper presents a TCN-BiGRU-SE deep learning model for sleep staging using instantaneous heart and breathing rates, achieving accuracies of 82.19% and 80.44% on two public datasets, outperforming single-modality approaches.

papers.title: White-matter disconnection shapes distributed cortical spectral dynamics after stroke
papers.summary: In acute stroke patients, perilesional cortex showed increased delta/theta and reduced beta power relative to controls. Structurally disconnected regions exhibited similar electrophysiological changes, including enhanced low-frequency activity and steeper aperiodic slopes, which correlated with neurological severity and behavioral impairment.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Self-Supervised Adaptation for EEG-FM under Fixed Computational Budgets
papers.summary: This study investigated parameter-efficient self-supervised adaptation for EEG foundation models, updating only 9% of parameters, and found consistent gains over linear probing, up to 20x AUCPR, across three clinical EEG datasets. Peak performance required only 20-50% of available unlabeled data, and performance depended on temporal window diversity rather than patient count.

papers.title: Genetic and Behavioral Variation Underlying an Integrated Temporal Phenotype in an Admixed South American Population
papers.summary: In a Uruguayan cohort, genetic variation in clock genes, particularly PER2 and BTRC, was associated with chronotype. A joint behavioral component correlated with DLMO and differed among genetic clusters, suggesting a complex interplay between behavioral and genetic factors.

papers.title: Biological rhythms, sleep disturbances, and the skin - a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes evidence linking sleep disturbances, circadian regulation, light exposure, and environmental factors to skin physiology, including barrier function, immune activity, and repair. It highlights that circadian disruption may contribute to skin aging, impaired repair, inflammatory dermatoses, and potential carcinogenesis.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity in Young Adults With Clinically Diagnosed Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Self-Reported Habitual Short Sleep: An Alpha-Band Network Analysis.
papers.summary: This study examined resting-state EEG functional connectivity in young adults with generalized anxiety disorder and habitual short sleep versus healthy controls. Results showed distributed alpha-band phase-based connectivity alterations, including stronger connectivity, higher global efficiency, and clustering in the GAD+HSS group, but no group differences in other bands or amplitude-based measures.

papers.title: Theta-range SEEG stimulation for intracranial mapping: extending conventional 1-Hz and 50-Hz protocols.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This study prospectively compared theta-range (7 Hz) electrical brain stimulation with conventional 1-Hz and 50-Hz protocols in temporal lobe SEEG mapping across 1,408 stimulations in 25 patients. At matched intensity and duration, 7-Hz stimulation elicited more afterdischarges and clinical signs than 1-Hz, and provided complementary information, supporting targeted evaluation of intermediate frequencies.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm of heart rate variability in tropical horses: age-associated autonomic alterations and environmental air pollution effects in an urban field setting.
papers.summary: This field study characterized 24-hour heart rate variability patterns in tropical horses, finding blunted circadian autonomic modulation, age-related reductions in parasympathetic activity, and negative correlations between air pollution (PM2.5, AQI) and HRV indices. It provides first evidence linking ambient air pollution with resting HRV alterations in horses.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG spectral power alterations following traumatic brain injury: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical and injury-related moderators.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified resting-state EEG spectral power changes after traumatic brain injury (TBI) from 24 studies, finding increased theta power in TBI compared to controls (g = 0.50). TBI etiology and sex moderated theta effects, but significance did not survive correction, and substantial heterogeneity was noted.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation as a modulator of thyroid function: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized 25 studies on the effects of sleep deprivation on thyroid function. Significant increases in TSH and free T3 were found, while free T4 changes were not significant, highlighting the sensitivity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis to sleep loss.

papers.title: Connecting the dots between sleep deprivation and obesity: the role of melatonin in appetite regulation and insulin sensitivity from a mechanistic review perspective.
papers.summary: This mechanistic review analyzed 82 studies to clarify links between sleep deprivation, appetite regulation, and insulin sensitivity, focusing on the role of melatonin. It suggests melatonin may improve insulin sensitivity and reduce body weight, but results are mixed and further research is needed.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic and neuroimaging prognosticators in pediatric FIRES with claustrum lesions: A 21-case retrospective study.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 21 pediatric FIRES patients with claustrum lesions found that acute-phase EEG showed characteristic dynamic changes, and absence of sleep spindles indicated more severe acute manifestations but did not predict long-term outcomes. Patients with isolated bilateral claustrum lesions had milder acute symptoms and better prognosis than those with concurrent thalamic/temporal lobe involvement.

papers.title: The circadian-microbiome-immune axis in colorectal cancer: mechanisms of spatiotemporal immunosuppression and chronotherapeutic horizons.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes preclinical evidence linking circadian disruption, gut microbiome changes (e.g., Lactobacillus depletion), and taurocholic acid-mediated RasGRF1/MAPK/ERK activation to rhythmic recruitment of PD-L1+ MDSCs, proposing a Temporal Immunosuppressive Shield (TIS) framework in colorectal cancer. It remains hypothesis-generating and not directly validated in human MSS CRC.

papers.title: Cognitive Impairment in isolated REM Sleep Behavior Disorder: a data-driven approach to understanding the heterogeneity of different phenotypes. A pilot study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional pilot study of 55 vPSG-confirmed iRBD patients found MCI in 60%, with data-driven clustering identifying three cognitive profiles (memory-executive, globally impaired, mild-preserved). Executive-attentional dysfunction was prominent, and TMT-B, TMT B-A, and MWCST perseverative errors best discriminated MCI status.

papers.title: A lifestyle-driven inflammatory load index and its circulating metabolomic signature identify susceptibility to hospital-recorded acute respiratory infections: a population-based cohort study of 295,679 adults.
papers.summary: In 295,679 UK Biobank participants, a lifestyle-anchored inflammatory load index (CII) showed graded associations with hospital-recorded ARIs (LRTI HR=1.56 for high vs low) and a circulating NMR-derived metabolomic risk signature accounted for ~19% of the association, dominated by fatty-acid biomarkers and GlycA. This suggests lifestyle-related inflammation contributes to ARI susceptibility.

papers.title: Regenerative Neural Stem Cell Therapy Improves Multidomain Neurological Deficits after Traumatic Brain Injury in Nonhuman Primates
papers.summary: This study tested a cryopreserved human neural stem cell product in a nonhuman primate TBI model, showing dose-dependent improvements in motor, cognitive, anxiety, and sleep-wake measures, with reduced lesion volume and no adverse events. Results support translational development.

papers.title: Fermented red quinoa alleviates sleep deprivation-induced anxiety-like behavior and inflammation associated with gut microbiota modulation.
papers.summary: This study in a mouse model showed that fermented red quinoa (RQF) alleviates sleep deprivation-induced anxiety-like behavior and inflammation, and modulates gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids. RQF may be a dietary strategy against sleep deprivation-induced neurobehavioral deficits.

papers.title: Expanding the interpretation of REM sleep without atonia in antidepressant users.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
papers.summary: This letter expands the interpretation of REM sleep without atonia in antidepressant users, likely discussing clinical considerations. However, no abstract was provided, so specific findings cannot be summarized.

papers.title: Circadian control of circulating tumour-derived extracellular vesicle secretion affects targeted therapy efficacy.
papers.summary: The authors introduce ctEV-CLOCK, a method to isolate nascent circulating tumour-derived extracellular vesicles with 12-hour resolution, revealing circadian oscillations in their abundance and protein profiles across mouse tumour models. Synchronizing targeted therapy with peak ctEV protein abundance markedly enhanced therapeutic efficacy, providing a framework for circadian-aligned cancer chronotherapy.

papers.title: Prevalence of Sleep Deprivation and its Associations with Depressive Symptoms, Academic Performance, and Sleep Hygiene among School-going Adolescents (12-18 Years) in Urban Delhi.
papers.journal: Indian journal of community medicine : official publication of Indian Association of Preventive & Social Medicine
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 1521 urban Indian adolescents, sleep deprivation prevalence was 22.5%, and was associated with lower academic grades, higher depressive symptoms, and poor sleep hygiene, but not with cognitive function scores. Depression and sleep hygiene were significant correlates of SLD in multivariate analysis.

papers.title: Exploring generation Z nurses' experiences of shift work in intensive care units: A qualitative analysis.
papers.summary: This qualitative descriptive study of 30 Generation Z nurses in Italian ICUs found that shift work causes psychophysical imbalance and career uncertainty, mitigated by coping strategies and peer support. Organisational recognition and structured transition processes are needed to support well-being and retention.

papers.title: Electrophysiological readout of ACTH-related neuroendocrine-immunomodulatory treatment response in infantile epileptic spasms syndrome: suppression of scalp ripple propagation networks.
papers.summary: In a retrospective multicenter study of 61 children with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome, ACTH therapy responders showed marked suppression of scalp ripple propagation network strength, with post-treatment network metrics differentiating responders from nonresponders (AUC ~0.90).

papers.title: Refractory Hyperammonemic Encephalopathy as a Paraneoplastic Presentation of Fibrolamellar Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Case Report.
papers.journal: The American journal of case reports
papers.summary: This case report describes a 24-year-old man with metastatic fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma who developed refractory hyperammonemic encephalopathy due to an acquired urea cycle disorder, indicated by depleted urea cycle intermediates and elevated urinary orotic acid. Despite treatment with ammonia scavengers and renal replacement therapy, the patient died, highlighting the poor prognosis and need for early multidisciplinary and palliative care.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
